passages.title: Discussion Text: Weighing Two Sides
passages.text: Should schools encourage students to travel without private cars? Supporters say walking, cycling, and public transport can reduce some transport emissions and may ease traffic near school gates. However, critics point out that long distances, bad weather, and unsafe routes can make these options difficult. They argue that a single rule would not fit every family. A balanced proposal is to improve bicycle parking and information about bus routes first, while allowing flexibility for students whose journeys are less straightforward.

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the discussion?
choices: Private cars are always the fastest choice
Lower-emission travel has benefits, but students’ situations differ
Every student lives within walking distance
Buses have no role in school travel
